close_reason: External oracle test added: Python cryptography generates sig, Rust verify_x_sig verifies it. extract_sig_header excision confirmed correct against independent vector.
description: In x_sig.rs::sign_article (test helper), the signature is computed over the original article_bytes (before the sig header is inserted). In verify_x_sig, verification uses article_without_sig (bytes with the sig header excised). These are the same only if the sig header is appended in the exact location that extract_sig_header later excises. However sign_article inserts the sig header immediately before the final CRLF separator, while extract_sig_header removes the header line using byte offsets in the UTF-8 header section. If a signed article is modified (e.g. extra whitespace) or if sign_article's insert_at offset does not match extract_sig_header's excise range exactly, verification will fail. The test oracle (sign then verify) is not an independent oracle — it can mask off-by-one bugs in the round-trip. There are no test vectors from an external signing tool (openssl, python-cryptography).
title: verify: X-Stoa-Sig signs article-without-sig-header but sign_article signs original bytes
